discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can turn an ordinary band insulator into a new state of matter, the quantum spin Hall insulator, characterized by a Z2 topological invariant protected by time-reversal symmetry, with helical edge states immune to backscattering. Molenkamp and collaborators (2007) observed this state in HgTe quantum wells through quantized edge conductance, establishing that band topology is a real, measurable property of materials. The idea generalized at once to three-dimensional topological insulators, now confirmed in many compounds by transport and photoemission, and became the foundation of topological materials science: Weyl semimetals, topological superconductors, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and the classification of symmetry-protected phases. It revealed that the Berry-phase geometry of Bloch electrons, not only symmetry breaking, organizes the phases of solids, a principle that has reshaped condensed matter physics and opened routes to dissipationless electronics and topological quantum computation.
